name: Facial Flex

card.summary: A resistance-band jaw and facial exerciser held in the mouth and squeezed against tension, promoted for firmer cheeks, jawline and neck.
card.note: Published research is a small study of four people and a short 1994 report; results on muscle activity were mixed.

quick.overview:
Facial Flex is a hand-held resistance device made by Facial Concepts, Inc. A flexible band with a mouthpiece sits between the lips, and the user pulls and pushes against its tension to exercise the muscles of the lips, cheeks, jaw and neck. It is marketed for a firmer-looking lower face and jawline.
The device was first developed as a treatment for microstomia, a tightening of the mouth after deep facial burns, and was later sold to the general public. Published work includes a small 8-week study of four healthy adults and a 1994 report on sagging facial muscles.
quick.how: Users place the device in the mouth and perform repeated squeezes against the resistance, typically in short sessions over several weeks. In the 8-week study, participants trained with a fixed resistance and were tested on how many repetitions and how long an isometric contraction they could manage.
quick.risks: No adverse events from the device have been reported. As with any strong, repeated jaw exercise, people with jaw joint (TMJ) problems are generally advised to check with a clinician before starting. Mouth-held devices should be kept clean.

lead: Facial Flex (also written Facial-Flex) is a resistance exerciser for the muscles of the face, jaw and neck, made by Facial Concepts, Inc. of Blue Bell, Pennsylvania. [1] It is promoted for toning the cheeks, jawline and neck.

How it helps looks: the idea is to build tone in the muscles around the mouth and jaw, with the aim of a more defined lower face. The manufacturer describes it as made of surgical-grade steel and a durable synthetic material. [2]

Research includes a 1994 report in the Journal of Geriatric Dermatology on a mechanically aided resistance exercise program for sagging facial muscles [2] and a 2002 study of the device in four healthy people over eight weeks [1].

angle.text: The device is used to give the muscles around the mouth and jaw a workout under resistance. Users hope the added tone shows as a firmer jawline and lower face.

Held in the mouth; pulled/squeezed against tension

paras: The Facial-Flex was created as a treatment for microstomia, a severe restriction of mouth opening caused by deep facial burns, and was subsequently applied in work on speech and facial-nerve disorders and sold as a consumer exerciser. [1]
It consists of a flexible band with a mouth piece, so that squeezing the lips and cheeks around it stretches the band against its tension, creating a form of resistance training for the lower face.

A 2002 paper in the International Journal of Orofacial Myology reported the first study of an 8-week mechanically aided facial exercise program with the Facial-Flex in four healthy adults. Lip muscle activity (EMG) and lip movements were recorded at two baseline sessions and after training. All four subjects increased their repetitions and the duration of isometric contraction on the device, but the physiological results were mixed: one subject showed the expected increase in normalized EMG activity along with greater movement range and peak velocity, one showed no systematic training effect, and two showed an increase in movement duration. [1]

A 1994 report in the Journal of Geriatric Dermatology by Grove, Rimdzius and Zerweck described a mechanically aided resistance exercise program for sagging facial muscles; its authors reported a reduction in biomechanical extensibility that matched participants' perception of firmer, more elastic skin. [2]

The device belongs to the family of jaw and face exercisers that appear in discussions of jawline definition, alongside chewing exercises, mastic gum and other jaw trainers. Masseter and neck muscle training is the usual rationale.

An 8-week study of the Facial-Flex in four healthy people is published. [1]
